claims.text: Post-deposition annealing of the FeNiCrCoCu coating will refine its grain structure.
Post-deposition annealing will promote formation of a protective surface oxide layer on the FeNiCrCoCu coating.
Annealing-induced grain refinement and oxide formation will lower the coating's high-temperature sliding wear rate.
Annealing-induced grain refinement and oxide formation will reduce microscopic deformation during high-temperature sliding.
The as-deposited baseline coating has minimal grain refinement.
The as-deposited baseline coating has minimal surface oxide development.
Controlled high-temperature annealing can induce grain refinement while maintaining the coating's overall phase composition.
Thermally driven grain-boundary evolution creates an ultra-nanocrystalline or amorphous near-surface layer.
Thermally driven microstructural evolution is coupled with formation of a stable protective oxide film.
Annealing activates grain-boundary migration that refines the near-surface grain structure.
Near-surface grain refinement facilitates dynamic amorphization under sliding stress.
The proposed microstructural changes reduce dislocation activity.
Reduced dislocation activity and the protective oxide prevent severe wear-induced damage during high-temperature sliding.
Annealed coatings will show less plastic deformation or delamination than unannealed coatings during high-temperature sliding.
The predicted benefit is limited to a high-temperature regime in which thermal activation significantly affects microstructural evolution and wear.
The predicted annealing benefit may not occur at lower sliding temperatures.
